To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the noncommutative spacetimes are covariant under affine transformations, (ii) covariance is lost if the spacetime transformations are generated by differential operators of order larger than one and (iii) covariance cannot be restored by a twist deformation

(i) the noncommutative product is not covariant under spacetime transformations; (ii) the noncommuting coordinates are not the generators of spacetime symmetrries; (iii) the Moyal product can be covariantized by introducing an ( x, Theta)-space, where the coordinates and the non-commuting coordinates are on the same footings; (iv) the noncommu-tivity matrix components are not the generators for noncommutative symmetries
the noncommutative Minkowski space is not a covariant space, and that it cannot be twisted into a covariant space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the noncommutative Moyal spacetime is covariant under spacetime translations and boosts.
the question of whether the noncommutative spacetimes are endowed with a noncommutatively covariant structure.
the question of whether the covariance of the star product can be extended to nontrivial spacetime transformations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Moyal deformation of spacetime symmetrries, as well as of their enveloping algebras, can be consistently described by the twist formalism, provided that one restricts the transformations to those generated by differential operators of order at most equal to one.
the twist-deformation is a covariant deformation of the Poincaré algebra, but it is not a covariant deformation for the affine algebra.
the Moyal algebra is covariant but not twisted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found the noncommutative spacetimes which are invariant under linear transformations and that these are the same as those invariant under the twist-deformed algebra.
the twist-deformation is a convenient mathematical tool to describe the noncommutative spacetimes, but it does not provide a satisfactory physical description of noncommutative quantum fields. In
the Moyal star product is a noncommutativization of the covariant point-wise product of functions on the spacetime manifold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to the twist-deformed case, covariance under spacetime transformations is a property of noncommutative quantum field theories, not of the noncommutative spacetimes they live in.
the Moyal deformation of the spacetime algebra is not an algebra deformation but an operator deformation.
the twist deformation is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for covariance of the Moyal product under spacetime transformations.
